slides.h: Could Hawking radiation prove this? No — it fails 4 separate ways.
b: The right instinct: it is the one quantum handle a black hole cosmology plausibly has.
2 of the 4 failures are structural — no telescope ever built, or ever imagined, changes them.

slides.h: The authors of the model never mention it
b: The name Hawking appears twice in their paper — both times in the list of references at the back.
Nowhere in the argument itself.

slides.h: Their horizon is a white hole horizon, not a black hole horizon
b: Hawking's calculation is for a black hole formed by collapse. A white hole is the time reverse — the opposite case.
And they fix the direction of time deliberately, by an entropy condition, in the direction that rules Hawking's setup out.

slides.h: They feed the temperature of the background light in as a given
b: It is an input to the solution.
A model that is handed the temperature cannot also predict it.

slides.h: It distinguishes nothing: a factor of exactly 2
b: Hawking temperature of the mass inside our horizon: 1.3 times 10 to the minus 30 degrees above absolute zero.
Ordinary cosmology, with no black hole in it, already predicts 2.7 times 10 to the minus 30 for its own horizon.
A perfect thermometer of unlimited sensitivity could not tell the two pictures apart.

slides.h: One wave is 15.9 times the radius of the observable universe
b: Not a single wave fits inside the part of the universe we can see.
No apparatus inside our horizon can measure a wave longer than our horizon — not a funding problem.
And 15.9 is the same whichever expansion rate you use, so the disagreement about that rate does not touch it.

slides.h: 10 to the minus 122 of the light we actually see
b: Evaporation would take 10 to the 125 times the age of the universe.
For the background light to BE Hawking radiation: about 0.6 of the mass of the Moon, with a horizon 67 millionths of a metre across.

slides.h: The same missing physics defeats both tests
b: Writing that temperature down at all assumes vacuum outside the wall. This model has fluid out there.
So you add physics the papers do not contain, then report a property of what you added — exactly the error I was failed for this afternoon.
Not a coincidence. The finding getting harder.

slides.h: Not that the tests are difficult — the theory does not contain enough physics to say what they would show
b: Unchanged since this afternoon, and now resting on more.
